candidate.answerReason: A constant function has derivative zero everywhere, including at x=5.

methods.label: Use the constant-function rule
methods.explanation: The derivative of a constant is \(0\).
methods.levelReason: The constant-function derivative rule is explicitly included in this elective unit.

methods.label: Use the horizontal graph
methods.explanation: The graph of \(f(x)=7\) is the horizontal line \(y=7\), so its tangent at \((5,7)\) is that same line. Its slope is \(0\); since a derivative equals the tangent slope, \(f'(5)=0\).
methods.levelReason: This uses the geometric meaning of the derivative and earlier knowledge of horizontal graphs, without additional differentiation rules.
